title: Expression of Regret at the Conduct of Mr Pritam Singh and Consideration of His Suitability to Continue as the Leader of The Opposition
what_it_is: Expression of Regret at the Conduct of Mr Pritam Singh and Consideration of His Suitability to Continue as the Leader of The Opposition

sections.label: Debate scope on Pritam Singh
sections.summary: Members must confine debate to Mr Pritam Singh's conduct and suitability, not reopen the court case or discuss other Members' conduct.

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: The main subject matters under discussion are the conduct of Mr Pritam Singh and his suitability to continue as the Leader of the Opposition.

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: Hon Members are reminded that they should confine their observations to the subject matter of the Motion and not to shift the debate to other unrelated incidents or political issues.

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: Furthermore, as this Motion is about the conduct of Mr Pritam Singh and other persons named in the Motion, and only to such extent, Members should refrain from raising and discussing the conduct of other Members as it is not directly relevant to the Motion.

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: While reference can be made to the judgment of the Court to set the context for the debate on today's Motion, the intent of this Motion is not to reopen the case, to dispute the findings of the Court or to question its decisions or to discuss the conduct of the trial.

sections.label: High Court upheld Singh's conviction
sections.summary: The High Court upheld Mr Pritam Singh's conviction on two counts of lying before the COP, confirming he guided Ms Raeesah Khan to maintain her lie.

sentences.speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: Last month, on 4 December 2025, the High Court upheld Mr Pritam Singh's conviction by the District Court on two counts of lying before the COP.

sentences.speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: The District Court also found that Mr Singh had guided Ms Raeesah Khan to maintain her lie to Parliament, confirming the COP's findings.

sections.label: Honesty and integrity affirmed
sections.summary: The passage affirms that honesty and integrity are fundamental pillars of Singapore's parliamentary and political system.

sentences.speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: Affirm that honesty and integrity are fundamental pillars of Singapore's parliamentary and political system; 2.

sections.label: Singh unsuitable as Opposition Leader
sections.summary: The passage considers his conduct renders him unsuitable to hold the Office of the Leader of the Opposition, which would undermine Parliament's standing and public confidence.

sentences.speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: Consider that such conduct renders him unsuitable to continue to hold the Office of the Leader of the Opposition, a Parliamentary leadership position with important responsibilities, duties and privileges, and that his continuation in this role would undermine the standing of Parliament and public confidence in the integrity of Singapore's political system; 5.

sections.label: Conviction and appeal dismissed
sections.summary: The District Court convicted Mr Singh in February 2025 for lying before the COP, and the High Court dismissed his appeal last month.

sentences.speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: In February 2025, the District Court convicted Mr Singh for lying before the COP.

sentences.speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: Last month, the High Court dismissed Mr Singh's appeal and upheld the findings of guilt on his charges.

sections.label: Singh told Khan to hide
sections.summary: Regarding Ms Khan's Untruth, Mr Singh told her to "take it to the grave", instructing her to hide the Untruth.

sentences.speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: First, in relation to Ms Khan's Untruth, Mr Singh told her to "take it to the grave", essentially instructing her to hide the Untruth.

sections.label: Singh repeated lying
sections.summary: Mr Singh lied repeatedly to the COP, the public and the Courts, doubling down each time.

sentences.speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: Mr Singh not only lied, but lied repeatedly – to the COP, to the public and to the Courts, doubling down each time.

sections.label: WP leaders recommend expulsion
sections.summary: On 30 November 2021, Mr Singh, Ms Lim and Mr Faisal recommended Ms Khan be expelled within 24 hours if she did not resign; she resigned that day.

sentences.speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: On 30 November 2021, Mr Singh, Ms Lim and Mr Faisal recommended to the WP CEC that for lying to Parliament, Ms Khan should be expelled from the party within 24 hours if she did not resign.

sentences.speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: Ms Khan resigned from the WP that same day.

sections.label: Singh convicted for false answers
sections.summary: Mr Singh was charged and convicted by the District Court for wilfully giving false answers.

sentences.speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: For wilfully giving these false answers, Mr Singh was charged and eventually convicted by the District Court.

sections.label: Singh leadership failure
sections.summary: The case shows a failure of leadership by Mr Singh, who is also the Leader of the Opposition.

sentences.speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: And that, is a problem as Mr Singh is also the Leader of the Opposition.

sentences.speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: This case shows a failure of leadership on the part of Mr Singh.

sections.label: Police reviewed assault cases
sections.summary: The Police combed through more than 1,400 sexual assault and related cases from 2018 to 2021 to investigate the false claims.

sentences.speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: The Police had to comb through more than 1,400 sexual assault and related cases from 2018 to 2021 to investigate the false claims.

sections.label: High Court decision date
sections.summary: In Mr Singh's own case, the High Court issued its decision on 4 December 2025.

sentences.speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: In contrast, in Mr Singh's own case, the High Court issued its decision on 4 December 2025.

sections.label: WP conference and disciplinary panel
sections.summary: The WP confirmed members requested a Special Cadre Members' Conference, then announced a disciplinary panel on Mr Singh.

sentences.speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: On 28 December 2025, the WP confirmed that some of its members had requested for a Special Cadre Members' Conference (CMC).

sentences.speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: On 3 January 2026, one whole month after the High Court judgment, the WP announced that a DP would be formed to determine if Mr Singh had contravened the party constitution.

sections.label: Leader's remarks on Singh
sections.summary: A speaker asks the Leader to confine her remarks to the Court's actual findings against Mr Singh.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat
sentences.text: The Leader has stated that Mr Singh has lied to the Courts and lied to Singaporeans.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat
sentences.text: The Court conviction was specifically for lying to the COP under oath, no perjury charge was brought.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat
sentences.text: These characterisations impute improper motives beyond the Court's actual findings.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat
sentences.text: I ask that the Leader confine her remarks to what the Court actually found.

sections.label: Motion on Singh's conduct
sections.summary: The passage states Mr Singh's conduct was dishonourable and urges Members to vote for the Motion.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: When the Office of the Leader of the Opposition was first introduced, there were high hopes for the role and how it would enhance the functioning and standing of Parliament.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: But now Mr Singh has done all the things that I have set out and been convicted in Court for lying to a Committee of Parliament.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: Under these circumstances, the conclusion is clear and beyond doubt: Mr Singh's conduct was dishonourable and unbecoming of an MP; and he has fallen short of the requirements and standards expected of the Leader of the Opposition.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: If Members agree with this conclusion, they should vote in favour of the Motion.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: If they disagree and wish to vote against, they should justify to this House and to Singaporeans why Singapore should accept such lowered standards of honesty and integrity from their political leaders.

sections.label: MPs resigned seats for accountability
sections.summary: MPs resigned their seats as party discipline and to express remorse, accountability and maintain public office standards.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: In all of these cases, the MPs resigned their seats as matter of party discipline, and to express remorse and accountability, but most of all to maintain the high standards expected of those in public office.

sections.label: Upholding standards and public confidence
sections.summary: Supporting the Motion shows MPs will uphold rigorous standards and prevent erosion of public confidence in institutions.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: If Parliament allows these standards to slip, distrust will gradually take root, and the public confidence in our institutions will be eroded, inevitably and irreversibly.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: By supporting this Motion, Members will show that this generation of MPs are determined never to allow that to happen and that we will continue to uphold and enforce the rigorous standards that have served Singapore well and will continue to do so for many years to come.

sections.label: District Court judgment on concealment
sections.summary: The District Court judgment stated the three WP leaders acted to conceal their involvement in guiding Ms Khan.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: The District Court judgment at paragraph 489 stated that the three WP leaders had acted to "conceal their involvement in guiding Ms Khan to maintain the Untruth since 8 August 2021". "Conceal", if one looks in the general meaning of the dictionary usually means cover-up.

sections.label: Denial of telling Khan
sections.summary: Raeesah Khan was not told to take her lie to the grave on 8 August 2021, and the speaker's conscience remains clear.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Raeesah Khan was not told to take her lie to the grave on 8 August 2021.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: My conscience remains clear, as it will forever, that this was not said by me to Khan at any point in time.

sections.label: Disagreement with dishonourable conduct finding
sections.summary: The speaker disagrees that their conduct was dishonourable and unbecoming of an MP, and disagrees with the Courts' and COP's finding of guilt.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Nobody is saying that." Court: "Correct." On Resolution 2, I disagree that my conduct was dishonourable and unbecoming of an MP, as I disagree with the finding of guilt by the Courts and the COP.

sections.label: Request to Public Prosecutor rejected
sections.summary: The speaker wrote to the PP seeking permission to refer to undisclosed statements for today's Parliamentary Motion, but the request was rejected.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: I wrote to the PP seeking permission to refer to these undisclosed statements for the purposes of today's Parliamentary Motion.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: However, my request was rejected by the PP.

sections.label: Parliament not re-litigating case
sections.summary: The speaker states that Parliament today is not re-litigating the case.

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: As I stated from the onset, Parliament today, we are not re-litigating the case.

sections.label: Relevant provision section 225A
sections.summary: The relevant provision is section 225A of the Criminal Procedure Code, and the speaker has a copy of it.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
sentences.text: The relevant provision is section 225A of the Criminal Procedure Code and I have a copy of it here.

sections.label: Permission needed for statements
sections.summary: The PP has to be informed or permission granted to use those statements outside of criminal proceedings.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
sentences.text: So, to answer the Minister's question, these are the relevant provisions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
sentences.text: And the PP has to be informed, or permission has to be granted from him to use those statements outside of criminal proceedings.

sections.label: Judiciary and Parliament as organs
sections.summary: The Speaker notes the Judiciary and Parliament are both organs of state and will rule later on the request.

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: Indeed, it is true that the Judiciary is one organ of state and likewise, the Parliament is another organ of state.

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: So, Mr Singh, if I may request you to continue with your speech, I will study this further and I will make a ruling on your request at a later stage.

sections.label: Conscience clear, responsibility for delay
sections.summary: He says his conscience is clear on both convictions but takes full responsibility for not quickly correcting Khan's lie.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
sentences.text: In my case, my conscience will always be clear insofar as my conviction on both charges is concerned.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
sentences.text: However, as I iterated in my public remarks after the judgment was given, I take full responsibility for not responding quickly enough to correct Khan's lie in her speech on women's empowerment in Parliament on 3 August 2021.

sections.label: Rejecting Resolution 3 of Motion
sections.summary: He says his timeframe was shorter, he acted for the MP and Parliament, and rejects Resolution 3.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
sentences.text: My timeframe was far shorter and I tried to do what I deemed was best for the MP in question and for Parliament, with a view to work towards an outcome where the MP took ownership and responsibility for her actions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
sentences.text: I certainly did not expect the MP to double down on her lie when asked about it, so I reject Resolution 3 of the Motion.

sections.label: Rejecting Resolutions 4 and 5
sections.summary: He rejects Resolution 4 and says no action should be taken against Sylvia Lim and Faisal Manap.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
sentences.text: I have done my best to work with my colleagues to advance the interests of Singaporeans with the WP as a responsible Opposition through the office.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
sentences.text: I reject Resolution 4, which flows from Resolutions 2 and 3.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
sentences.text: On Resolution 5, I take the view that no action should be taken against my colleagues, Sylvia Lim and Faisal Manap, as I do not agree with the judgement and the findings of the COP.

sections.label: Explaining his legal background
sections.summary: He says he has not met most Parliamentary colleagues and explains he has practised as an advocate and solicitor over 30 years.

sentences.speaker: Ms Kuah Boon Theng (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Indeed, I have not had the chance to meet with most of my Parliamentary colleagues, so with your permission, Mr Speaker, I would like to briefly explain my own background.

sentences.speaker: Ms Kuah Boon Theng (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I am an advocate and solicitor who has been in practice for over 30 years.

sections.label: Professions, honour and integrity
sections.summary: He says disciplinary proceedings enforce standards and communicate values, and professionals are called to act with honour and integrity.

sentences.speaker: Ms Kuah Boon Theng (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In this regard, formal disciplinary proceedings provide not only a means for a profession to enforce its standards, but also an avenue for it to communicate to the public, as well as to underscore to its members, the values and ethos which undergird its work." The point I wish to make is this – anyone who has taken the Hippocratic Oath and been conferred the privileges of medical practice, and anyone who has been brought up in the best traditions of the bar, and that includes the Leader of the Opposition, will know very well that we are called by our profession to act with honour and integrity.

sections.label: Standards for Parliamentarians' conduct
sections.summary: Standards of conduct for Parliamentarians cannot be lower than those expected of legal or medical professionals.

sentences.speaker: Ms Kuah Boon Theng (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Surely, the standards of conduct for the profession of Parliamentarians cannot be lower than that which is expected from the legal or medical professional.

sections.label: Holding conduct to account
sections.summary: To retain public trust, behaviour falling short of standards must be called out, held to account and sanctioned, citing Justice Steven Chong's decision.

sentences.speaker: Ms Kuah Boon Theng (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: To retain the trust and confidence of the public, we must be prepared to call out behaviour and conduct that has fallen short of those standards, hold people to account and consider appropriate sanction or measures that must be taken.

sentences.speaker: Ms Kuah Boon Theng (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In considering this Motion, we look to the decision of Justice of the Court of Appeal, Steven Chong, who dismissed the appeal lodged by the Leader of the Opposition and upheld the conviction on two charges of wilfully giving false answers to a Parliamentary Committee of Privileges.

sections.label: Motion on Pritam Singh's conduct
sections.summary: The Motion's other paragraphs ask Members to indicate if they agree Pritam Singh's conduct was dishonourable and renders him unsuitable as Leader of the Opposition.

sentences.speaker: Ms Kuah Boon Theng (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The other paragraphs of the Motion that relate to Mr Pritam Singh’s conduct calls on each of us to indicate if we agree with the characterisation of that conduct as dishonourable and unbecoming of an MP, and whether Mr Pritam Singh’s conviction and conduct render him unsuitable to continue as the Leader of the Opposition, on grounds that his continuation in this role would undermine the standing of Parliament and public confidence in the integrity of Singapore’s political system.

sections.label: Invitation to Pritam Singh
sections.summary: Members are asked to agree Pritam Singh's conduct was dishonourable and his continuation undermines Parliament, and he is invited to reflect and give up the position.

sentences.speaker: Ms Kuah Boon Theng (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In this Motion, Members are asked if we agree that Mr Pritam Singh’s conduct was indeed dishonourable and unbecoming of an MP, and that his continuation as Leader of the Opposition will undermine the standing of Parliament and public confidence in the integrity of our political system.

sentences.speaker: Ms Kuah Boon Theng (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I invite Mr Pritam Singh to reflect on his own conduct and indicate if he would be the first to agree that he has, indeed, fallen below the standards that should rightly be expected of him, and whether he would respond appropriately by voluntarily agreeing to give up the position of Leader of the Opposition.

sections.label: Court rulings and opposition figures
sections.summary: The Court ruled twice the Leader of the Opposition lied before the Committee of Privileges and guided a junior MP to continue lying, prompting today's Motion.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
sentences.text: The Court has ruled twice that the Leader of the Opposition lied before the Committee of Privileges and guided a junior MP to continue lying in Parliament, resulting in today's Motion for debate.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
sentences.text: From our founding Prime Minister, Mr Lee Kuan Yew, before the PAP formed the government, to Mr Chiam See Tong of Singapore People's Party and Mr Low Thia Kiang of WP, our Parliament has never lacked in respectable opposition figures.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
sentences.text: Therefore, after the 2020 General Election, a formal role for the Leader of the Opposition was established, since held by WP's Mr Pritam Singh.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
sentences.text: Despite our political differences and party affiliations, Mr Low is indeed a respected political leader.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
sentences.text: Therefore, witnessing the current situation where the Leader of the Opposition has been ruled by the Court as dishonest towards Parliament and having guided his junior party member Raeesah Khan to continue covering lies in Parliament is disheartening.

sections.label: Credibility and taking a stand
sections.summary: Ensuring Parliament maintains a high level of credibility is paramount, so all MPs must take a stand on the Motion.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
sentences.text: However, to achieve this goal, ensuring that Parliament maintains a high level of credibility is paramount.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
sentences.text: Thus, as we consider the Motion before us, it is necessary for all MPs to take a stand.

sections.label: Conviction findings and parliamentary leadership
sections.summary: The conviction and COP findings are part of the public and legal record and must be respected, and no Member stands above the law.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The conviction and the findings of the COP now form part of the public and legal record, and they must be respected.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The question before this House is therefore not to revisit the facts, but to reflect on what these findings mean for a Parliamentary leadership position that carries distinct responsibilities and expectations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I affirm, without reservation, the principle that no Member of this House stands above the law and that honesty before Parliament and its Committees is non-negotiable.

sections.label: Support for the Motion
sections.summary: Having considered the principle and the responsibilities of Parliamentary leadership, the speaker supports the Motion to uphold Parliament's integrity and standing.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: For that reason, Mr Speaker, having considered both the principle at stake and the responsibilities attached to Parliamentary leadership, I support the Motion.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: It reflects fidelity to the role I was appointed to play and to the responsibility this House bears – to uphold the integrity and standing of Parliament.

sections.label: 2022 referral to the PP
sections.summary: Parliament in 2022 referred Mr Singh and Mr Faisal Manap to the PP, who prosecuted Mr Singh.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
sentences.text: Parliament had, in 2022, referred Mr Singh and Mr Faisal Manap to the PP, who proceeded to prosecute Mr Singh.

sections.label: Resolution five on implications
sections.summary: Resolution five states the High Court judgment and COP findings have implications for Mr Faisal Manap and the speaker to be considered separately.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
sentences.text: Resolution five states that the High Court judgment and the COP's findings have implications on Mr Faisal Manap and myself, which have to be considered separately.

sections.label: No opportunity to present side
sections.summary: The Prosecution was solely against Mr Singh, and Mr Faisal and the speaker were not called as witnesses, so had no opportunity to present their side.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
sentences.text: As the Prosecution was solely against Mr Singh, and Mr Faisal and I were not called as witnesses by either party, we had no opportunity to present our side of the story to the Court.

sections.label: Further steps under PPIPA
sections.summary: Any further steps Parliament wishes to take against the speaker must be based solely on the COP's conclusions and in accordance with PPIPA.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
sentences.text: For the reasons that I have just explained, if there are any further steps that Parliament wishes to take against me, it must be based solely on the COP's conclusions and in accordance with PPIPA.

sections.label: Advice to continue work
sections.summary: They advised the speaker to take good care of themselves and stressed the importance of continuing their work, which they will keep doing and strive to do better.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
sentences.text: They have advised us to take good care of ourselves and at the same time, emphasised how important it was for us to continue our work.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
sentences.text: We will continue our work and strive to do even better for them.

sections.label: Whip lifted for WP MPs
sections.summary: The Leader of the Opposition and WP Whip, Mr Pritam Singh, lifted the whip on this debate, letting each WP MP speak and vote freely by conscience and facts.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The Leader of the Opposition and WP's Whip, Mr Pritam Singh, has lifted the whip on this debate, allowing each WP MP to speak and vote freely, according to their own conscience and their assessment of the facts before them.

sections.label: Findings against Lim and Faisal
sections.summary: The speaker says it is difficult to hold findings in a judgment against the Leader of the Opposition against Ms Lim or Mr Faisal, as neither participated in the trial or presented evidence.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Regarding paragraph 5 on Ms Sylvia Lim and Mr Faisal Manap, it is difficult for me to see how the findings in a judgment against the Leader of the Opposition can be held against Ms Lim or Mr Faisal, considering neither of them participated in the trial, nor presented their own evidence in Court.

sections.label: Motion as political penalty
sections.summary: By seeking to remove his position as Leader of the Opposition, the Motion appears to impose a further political penalty on top of a legal one.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: By seeking to remove his position as the Leader of the Opposition, this Motion appears to be imposing a further political penalty on top of a legal one.

sections.label: WP MPs outnumbered in Parliament
sections.summary: The WP is vastly outnumbered in this House, with 12 WP MPs compared to 87 PAP MPs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The WP is vastly outnumbered in this House.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: There are 12 WP MPs in this Parliament, compared to 87 PAP MPs.

sections.label: Tan Chuan-Jin resignation affair
sections.summary: In July 2023, Mr Tan Chuan-Jin resigned as Speaker over an affair with a sitting MP, which the Prime Minister had known about since late 2020.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat
sentences.text: In July 2023, Mr Tan Chuan-Jin resigned as Speaker over an affair with a sitting MP.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat
sentences.text: The Prime Minister had known since late 2020 – nearly three years.

sections.label: Motion treatment of PAP versus WP
sections.summary: The passage asks why Parliament was never asked to judge Mr Tan Chuan-Jin, but a Motion is brought for Mr Pritam Singh.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat
sentences.text: So, the Member who faced nothing gets a quiet exit and the Member who already faced the Courts must now face Parliament as well.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat
sentences.text: So, if this Motion represents the proper standard for addressing misconduct by Parliamentary leaders, why was Parliament never asked in those three years to judge Mr Tan Chuan-Jin?

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat
sentences.text: What justifies a Motion for Mr Pritam Singh of the WP, but not Mr Tan Chuan-Jin of the PAP?

sections.label: High Court findings on Singh
sections.summary: The passage states the High Court found Mr Singh hoped not to deal with the Untruth and gave false testimony to the COP.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education and Minister for National Development (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
sentences.text: The honourable High Court judge said that, "From the time he, Mr Singh, learnt about the Untruth on 7 August 2021, till the time when it was decided that Ms Khan should clarify the Untruth on 11 October 2021, the appellant was hoping that he would not have to deal with it." The judgment also noted that the WP leaders were trying to manage risks of admitting to the Untruth, considering whether the Untruth would be raised again, and would the Government be able to discover the Untruth.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education and Minister for National Development (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
sentences.text: It also concluded that Mr Pritam Singh did not intend, and I quote: "did not intend that Ms Khan should clarify the Untruth, and that he had given false testimony to the COP by claiming that he did." Though he maintains his assertion of innocence, Mr Singh has said previously he accepted the Court judgment fully and without reservation.

sections.label: Singh's actions fell short
sections.summary: The passage states Mr Singh failed to guide his colleague, take responsibility, and respect Parliament and the Leader of the Opposition office.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education and Minister for National Development (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
sentences.text: In this case, Mr Singh's actions fell short.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education and Minister for National Development (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
sentences.text: First in failing to guide his young Parliamentary colleague to do the right thing when she first erred; second, in not taking responsibility for his own actions; and third, in not respecting the institution of Parliament and the office of the Leader of the Opposition.

sections.label: Singh gave false testimony
sections.summary: The passage states the High Court ruled Mr Singh did not tell the truth to the Committee of Privileges.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education and Minister for National Development (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
sentences.text: Second, there is now no longer any doubt or uncertainty that Mr Pritam Singh has given false testimony, even though at that time he was under oath when appearing before the Committee of Privileges.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education and Minister for National Development (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
sentences.text: Following the court process, including the unsuccessful appeal at the High Court, Mr Pritam Singh has been given ample opportunity to clear the air and defend himself against the charges about his conduct.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education and Minister for National Development (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
sentences.text: However, the High Court has ruled that Mr Pritam Singh did not tell the truth to the Committee of Privileges.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education and Minister for National Development (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
sentences.text: A Member of Parliament was initially found to have lied in this Chamber, and with this knowledge, the Leader of the Opposition and party leader of the said Member of Parliament opted not to come clean expeditiously and immediately after the first untruth.

sections.label: Parliament should voice regret
sections.summary: The passage states Parliament should voice strong regret over Mr Pritam's actions and draw a line that this conduct is unacceptable.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education and Minister for National Development (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
sentences.text: Second, in accepting responsibility for his actions honestly, and third, in not respecting the institution of Parliament and the office of Leader of the Opposition.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education and Minister for National Development (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
sentences.text: It falls to Parliament to voice its strong regret over Mr Pritam's actions and conduct, to draw a line in the sand that this is unacceptable and has crossed that line, and that it does not reflect the conduct and character that is fundamentally demanded of Members of Parliament.

sections.label: Integrity and public confidence
sections.summary: The passage warns that allowing transgressions against honesty and integrity could erode Singapore's parliamentary and political system.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education and Minister for National Development (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
sentences.text: If we allow transgressions against the fundamental values of society and the pillars of our institutions, such as honesty, integrity, and honour, there is worry that over time, this will erode, taint and even destroy everything we have built together as one people in our parliamentary and political system.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education and Minister for National Development (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
sentences.text: There is a worry that a pot of milk could spoil because of a drop of indigo (Malay idiom that carries meaning similar to "one bad apple spoils the whole bunch"). : Mr Speaker, I conclude by drawing Members' attention to the fourth limb of the Motion, relating to the standing of Parliament and public confidence in the integrity of Singapore's political system.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education and Minister for National Development (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
sentences.text: I urge Members to reflect and consider carefully on the weight of this Motion, not only on the integrity of this House as an institution, but also on the signal that we send about where we as a Parliament and as a society stand on honesty and truth telling by our MPs and by all who hold positions of leadership.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education and Minister for National Development (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
sentences.text: That this Motion must come before the House today is regrettable.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Education and Minister for National Development (Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi)
sentences.text: But integrity is not something we can compromise on nor waver upon even in the slightest.

sections.label: Undertaking not to use material
sections.summary: The speaker notes that under section 225A of the Criminal Procedure Code, the recipient is deemed to have undertaken not to use the material for other purposes without the PP's permission.

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: I would just like to inform you of my considerations in reaching my decision.

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: I note that under section 225A of the Criminal Procedure Code, you are deemed to have given an undertaking to the Court not to use that material for any purpose other than the purpose of the criminal proceedings without the permission of the PP.

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: You had earlier informed the House that the PP has not given you permission to do so.

sections.label: Respecting undertaking between institutions
sections.summary: The speaker says allowing the request would impinge on mutual respect between institutions, so the document will not be allowed to be used.

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: If I were to allow for this request, it would impinge on the mutual respect and forbearance between our two institutions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: We will respect the undertaking you are deemed to have given to the Court, and therefore I will not allow that document to be used.

sections.label: Noting COP report and conviction
sections.summary: The speaker says Parliament already resolved to note the COP Report, and that members cannot agree on dishonourable conduct or the MP's suitability as Leader of the Opposition.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: Paragraph 2 calls on us to note the judgment where the High Court upheld Mr Singh's conviction for lying to the COP.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: Today, they have all had a problem noting the findings of the COP.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: But I think they may have forgotten that when the COP Report was actually presented to Parliament several years ago, Parliament actually did resolve to note the COP Report.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: So, this does not do anything more than call on Parliament to do something it has already done.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: But then, apart from that, having agreed that honesty and integrity are fundamental, having agreed that we must act with integrity at all times and respect and abide by the law, they are somehow unable to agree that lying to the COP and guiding an MP to continue with her Untruth to Parliament is dishonourable conduct and unbecoming of an MP or to express any regret about it.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: They are also unable to consider, or they find themselves unable to consider, that an MP who has been convicted by the Court for lying and for misconducting himself in the manner described is unsuitable for the role of the Leader of the Opposition.

sections.label: Singh's acceptance of judgments
sections.summary: The speaker says Mr Singh called the verdict disappointing but accepted it fully and without reservation, and now says he accepts the Courts but does not agree they are correct.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: Actually, at that time, he never said that he disagreed with the verdict.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: He just said it was disappointing and there is a big difference between saying that something is disappointing and saying that you disagree with it.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: But on record, he had said it was disappointing.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: Then he went on to say that he respected and accepted the judgment fully and without reservation.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: But today, he comes to Parliament to say that, actually, what he really means is that he just accepts that the Courts are there, but he does not agree that they are correct.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: And earlier, of course, you will notice when Mr Speaker made his ruling, Mr Singh also said that it was disappointing, but he accepted it fully and without reservation.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: So, I think we all know today that when Mr Singh tells you that he accepts what you say fully and without reservation, he means you are wrong.

sections.label: Cross-examination and court findings
sections.summary: The speaker says Mr Singh had the right to cross-examine witnesses and the fullest opportunity to argue his case, and both the District Court and High Court found he had lied to the COP.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: He had the right and the ability to cross-examine the witnesses, to show whether their evidence was really right or wrong.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: And the Courts listened to that, and the District Court could not accept what he said and found that he had lied to the COP.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: The High Court heard, again, the points which he wished to canvass, and he had the fullest opportunity to argue his case before the Courts; and the High Court, too, reached the same conclusion.

sections.label: Leader of Opposition lying on oath
sections.summary: The speaker says Parliament is left with a Leader of the Opposition who has been found guilty of two counts of lying on oath.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: The Courts have made a finding, and we are now left with a situation where, as a Parliament, we have a Leader of the Opposition who has been found guilty of two counts of lying on oath.

sections.label: Appellant's failure to follow up
sections.summary: The appellant's two-month failure to follow up on the Untruth is probative of the Grave Statement and his understanding.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: In this case, I find that the appellant's complete failure to follow up with Ms Khan or the other WP leaders on the Untruth for around two months after the 8 August meeting up unitl the 3 October Meeting is probative of the making of the Grave Statement during the 8 August Meeting and the appellant's prevailing understanding that there was no need to proactively clarify the Untruth in Parliament.

sections.label: Deferring decision on two points
sections.summary: Parliament said it would defer a decision on two points until the outcome of Mr Singh's case.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: For those two points, Parliament said, we would defer a decision on that until the outcome of Mr Singh's case.

sections.label: Court found statement made
sections.summary: The Court found the statement was made and that Ms Lim and Mr Faisal were present when it was made.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: She was not a witness, she was not a party to the Court proceedings.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: But the point is that the Court had found that the statement was made and that Ms Lim and Mr Faisal were present when it was made.

sections.label: Outstanding issues for Mr Faisal
sections.summary: Two outstanding issues for Mr Faisal were lying to the COP and guiding Ms Khan to hide the Untruth.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: Then, there were two other remaining outstanding issues with respect to Mr Faisal.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: These are similar to the ones for Ms Lim: one, for lying to the COP that the statement "take it to the grave" was not made; and secondly, for his involvement in guiding Ms Khan to hide the Untruth.

sections.label: Leader of Opposition convicted of lying
sections.summary: The Leader of the Opposition has been convicted of two counts of lying before a Committee of Parliament.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: They know that every time they go out and do business, people look at them and wonder, "You are a company and your CEO has been convicted for lying and dishonesty, what sort of company are you?" That is the issue that is being discussed here.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: We have a Parliament where you have the Leader of the Opposition, which is a significant position and role, who has been convicted of two counts of lying before a Committee of Parliament.

sections.label: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin asked to step down
sections.summary: In Mr Tan Chuan-Jin's case, he was asked to step down and told to resign his seat.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: In Mr Tan Chuan-Jin's case, he was asked to step down.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: As a matter of party discipline, he was told to resign his seat.

sections.label: Legal Profession Act referral
sections.summary: Section 94 of the Legal Profession Act provides that legal practitioners convicted of fraud or dishonesty may be referred, a matter for the Law Society, AGC and Courts.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: I think Ms Cassandra Lee had a question about the Legal Profession Act.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: I think the short answer to that is that under the Legal Profession Act, section 94 does provide that legal practitioners who have been convicted of an offence involving fraud or dishonesty may have to be referred, but that is a matter not for us but for the Law Society, for the AGC and for the Courts.

sections.label: Motion on Parliament integrity
sections.summary: The Motion concerns upholding Parliament's integrity and standing, MPs' conduct standards, and Members' responsibility to honour the people's trust.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: This Motion goes beyond an individual or party or their actions.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: This Motion is about upholding the integrity and standing of Parliament, upholding the standard of conduct of our MPs and how it reflects on our Parliament, and upholding our responsibilities as elected Members of this House to honour the trust of our people and always do the right thing by them, even if it is politically inconvenient to do so.

sections.label: Number of briefings
sections.summary: The speaker does not have the number of briefings, stating it was not a matter of quantity.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: With respect to the last point, I do not have the number of briefings, but it was not a matter of quantity.

sections.label: President not convicted of dishonesty
sections.summary: The President who opened this House was not convicted of any offence of dishonesty.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: The President who opened this House was not convicted of any offence of dishonesty.

sections.label: Conviction and Leader suitability
sections.summary: A conviction for lying before a COP and guiding a junior MP to lie questions suitability for Leader of the Opposition.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: And it does not mean that we cannot express a view on his suitability.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: And when you have a conviction for lying, before a COP and guiding a junior MP to lie, or to maintain an Untruth – that brings into question suitability for the position of a Leader of the Opposition.

sections.label: Singh case political treatment
sections.summary: The speaker addressed the difference that in Ms Raeesah's and Mr Leon Perera's cases, they admitted their wrongdoings.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
sentences.text: Whereas in Mr Singh's case, we seem to be acting "politically", or some words to that effect.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
sentences.text: So, actually, in my speech I had attempted to address this by saying that the difference there is that, in Ms Raeesah's case and as well as Mr Leon Perera's case, they admitted their wrongdoings.

sections.label: Lim and Faisal COP evidence
sections.summary: The COP found Ms Lim and Mr Faisal lied under oath about the Grave Statement telling Ms Khan to take it to the grave.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: It is correct that Ms Lim and Mr Faisal did not appear in the Court proceedings.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: But Ms Lim and Mr Faisal did appear and give evidence before the COP, and they gave evidence under oath.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: And the COP found that, in respect of the making of the Grave Statement, in other words, the telling of Ms Khan "to take it to the grave", the COP found that Ms Lim and Mr Faisal had lied about what had happened there.

sections.label: Position on Motion limbs
sections.summary: The speaker agrees with limbs one and six of the Motion and disagrees with limbs two to five.

sentences.speaker: Mr Low Wu Yang Andre
sentences.text: My position on all six limbs of the Motion is: I will I agree with limbs one and six of the Motion; and I do not agree with limbs two to five.

sections.label: Pritam Singh unsuitable as Opposition Leader
sections.summary: It considers Mr Pritam Singh's conviction and conduct make him unsuitable to continue as Leader of the Opposition.

sentences.text: Considers that Mr Pritam Singh’s conviction and conduct render him unsuitable to continue as the Leader of the Opposition, a Parliamentary leadership position carrying important responsibilities, duties and privileges, and that his continuation in this role would undermine the standing of Parliament and public confidence in the integrity of Singapore’s political system; 5.

sections.label: High Court upheld Pritam Singh conviction
sections.summary: The High Court upheld Mr Pritam Singh's conviction for lying to the Committee of Privileges and its findings on guiding Ms Raeesah Khan's lie.

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: SGHC 242 where the High Court upheld Mr Pritam Singh’s conviction for lying to the Committee of Privileges, and the findings of the Committee of Privileges that he had guided Ms Raeesah Khan to continue with her lie to Parliament; (proc text)]   [(proc text) 4.

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: Considers that Mr Pritam Singh’s conviction and conduct render him unsuitable to continue as the Leader of the Opposition, a Parliamentary leadership position carrying important responsibilities, duties and privileges, and that his continuation in this role would undermine the standing of Parliament and public confidence in the integrity of Singapore’s political system; (proc text)] [(proc text) 5.

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: Notes that the High Court judgment and the Committee’s findings have implications for Ms Sylvia Lim and Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap, which have to be considered separately; and (proc text)] [(proc text) 6.

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: Calls upon all Members of Parliament to uphold their solemn duty to respect and abide by the law, act with integrity at all times, and honour the trust placed in them by Singaporeans." (proc text)]
